context: a letter from W. E. Darwin, which you are answering
exchanges:
If you go to the Jermyn St Museum, I should be much obliged if you would ask the porter for the box containing the skull & bones belonging to Mr Cumberbatch, & get William to make the box up safe & send it to me by rail as Mr C. has asked me for it; if you do not go could you [send] William to get it. I unfortunately utterly forgot it when passing thro’.

I hope you are well enough to find London pleasant.

Your affect son | W E Darwin

I will mention your note to no one, not even to Mamma.—

I agree that you could not ask Lubbock.—

I first thought of Hensleigh W. who has acted as arbitrator, was Barrister & Magistrate & formerly Chairman of Price’s candles, Bread Coy &c.—but being a near relation would be I suppose fatal.

Could you & Mr Atherley ask Henry Bonham Carter: he is Barrister & I think Secretary of a great Insurance Coy.—

By far the best man would be George Norman, as Director of Bank of England & of high standing; but then I doubt whether I could ask such a favour.— If the arbitrator has to go into accounts I certainly could not.— If he & co-arbitrator were to meet in London & to agree over a statement previously admitted by both parties as correct, then I presume the trouble to the Arbitrators would not be great, & I think I could ask it, as an extraordinary favour.

I will keep subject in mind; but I do not think it likely that any other name wd occur to me.—

I hope to God it may succeed.— Let me hear how things go on— —

Yours affecty | C. Darwin
